title: Poppi wants its next employees to come from social media
tldr: Beverage brand Poppi is recruiting its next hires directly from social media creators, treating content skill as a core job qualification. A concrete case of employee-generated content and creator-native hiring blurring the line between marketing and workforce.
angle: When 'can you make content' becomes a job requirement: what employee-generated content means for how brands staff up.

title: Why Reese's Book Club is betting big on 'micro-communities'
tldr: Reese Witherspoon's book club is investing in small, in-person 'micro-community' events like Storyfest rather than chasing scale. A tangible case study in human-centered, community-first content strategy over reach metrics.
angle: The shift from audience size to intimacy: why brands are building micro-communities instead of megaphones.

title: The creator economy is headed for $500 billion, so why do their fans feel like a prison?
tldr: Fortune examines the darker psychology of fan communities as the creator economy scales, where parasocial bonds start to feel confining for audiences. A sharp lens on how people actually consume creator content.
angle: Parasocial fatigue: the audience-psychology cost of the $500B creator economy.

title: Dentsu taps microdrama trend for Co-op
tldr: Co-op launches its first microdrama with Dentsu, and MediaCat questions whether it's a genuinely new format or a rebrand of existing short-form serialized content. Useful skeptical read on a hyped format.
angle: Microdrama: real new format or repackaged soap opera? What brands should actually take from the trend.

title: How a Summer of Protests Upended India's Media
tldr: Celebrity news anchors in India are being displaced by celebrity YouTubers as protest coverage reshapes trust and audiences. A vivid case of media-consumption habits shifting from legacy TV to independent creators.
angle: When YouTubers replace anchors: what India's media upheaval says about where trust is migrating.

title: The Only Two Types of Content that AI Can Never Make
tldr: Orbit Media argues that original research and first-person experience are the two content types AI can't replicate, making them strategic differentiators. A crisp, actionable framing for human-centered content.
angle: The AI-proof content moat: why original research and lived experience are now your competitive edge.

title: Now that's what I call comms planning! Taco Bell's 'Guacabono'
tldr: A breakdown of the strategic thinking behind Taco Bell's 'Guacabono' campaign that's getting cultural traction right now. A tidy campaign case study in smart comms planning.
angle: Anatomy of a moment: what Taco Bell's Guacabono teaches about planning for cultural relevance.

title: AI Traffic Conversion Rates: New Research from 97 B2B Websites and 29M visits
tldr: Orbit Media's original study of 97 B2B sites and 29M visits reveals how AI-referred traffic actually converts. Fresh data for anyone rethinking content attribution in the AI-search era.
angle: Does AI traffic convert? What 29M visits reveal about the real ROI of AI search visibility.

title: How small brands can create standout campaigns without a big budget
tldr: PR Daily uses Therabody's 'Add Some Magic'—an ad shot in under four hours by an in-house team—to show how idea and collaboration beat budget. Concrete, replicable campaign case study.
angle: Four hours, no budget, big impact: the in-house creative playbook behind Therabody's campaign.

title: AI Visibility Starts With Trust—and You Can't AI Your Way Out of a Trust Problem
tldr: Gini Dietrich argues AI-visibility tools can't fix an underlying trust deficit, framing trust as a supply chain with unskippable stations. A useful counter-narrative to the AEO tool gold rush.
angle: You can't automate credibility: why AI visibility is downstream of earned trust.

title: USA Today Co. is reformatting content to attract more AI licensing deals
tldr: USA Today is restructuring its content specifically so AI bots can ingest it, chasing new licensing revenue. An early signal of publishers designing content for machines, not just humans.
angle: Writing for the bots: how content architecture is being reshaped for AI licensing revenue.

title: Brands Are Paying to Get Into AI Answers. Publishers Are Deleting the Pages That Put Them There.
tldr: A paradox emerging in AI search: brands pay to appear in AI answers while publishers delete the very pages that source them. Signals a coming tension over who controls AI-answer visibility.
angle: The vanishing sources: what happens to brand visibility when AI's underlying pages disappear.

title: Streaming giants are snagging podcast IP, which poses hidden challenges for brands
tldr: Streaming platforms acquiring podcast IP creates new friction for brands relying on podcast partnerships and audience access. Timely for anyone building a B2B or brand podcast strategy.
angle: Who owns the mic? What streaming's podcast IP grab means for brand podcast strategies.

title: As AI reshapes newsrooms, leading media outlets are charting different paths for its use
tldr: A comparison of how major outlets are adopting—or resisting—generative AI in editorial work, including the Guardian's strike-era deployment. Useful map of divergent content-governance approaches.
angle: No consensus on AI: what newsroom policy divergence signals for content governance everywhere.

title: Между нишей и массовостью: послание Натальи Брянцевой, Avgvst
tldr: An excerpt from a new book on building an 'authentic brand' from the heart, addressing how concept-driven businesses grow without losing identity. A founder-led take on authenticity vs. scale.
angle: Scaling without selling out: the authenticity tension every concept brand eventually hits.
